topics.name: Whole numbers up to 1 000 000
misconceptions: Learners may think a digit means the same thing wherever it is written, or round the wrong way when the digit to check is exactly 5.

topics.name: Addition and subtraction of larger numbers
misconceptions: Learners may line up numbers from the left instead of the right, or forget to carry and borrow when a column adds to more than nine.

topics.name: Multiplication and division of whole numbers
misconceptions: Learners may think multiplication always makes a number bigger, or forget to write the remainder when dividing.

topics.name: Multiples and factors
prerequisites: Multiplication and division of whole numbers
misconceptions: Learners may mix up multiples and factors, or think 1 is not a factor of every number.

topics.name: Time
misconceptions: Learners may confuse the hour hand and the minute hand, or think 100 minutes equal one hour.

topics.name: Common fractions
misconceptions: Learners may think a larger bottom number means a larger fraction, or only think of fractions as pieces of a pizza.

topics.name: Equivalent fractions
misconceptions: Learners may multiply only the top number to find an equivalent fraction, or think simplest form means making any numbers smaller.

topics.name: Perimeter and area
misconceptions: Learners may add all sides to find area, or think two shapes with the same perimeter must have the same area.

topics.name: Perimeter and area again
misconceptions: Learners may count the shared sides twice when finding the perimeter of two joined rectangles, or forget to measure area in square units.

topics.name: Decimal fractions
misconceptions: Learners may think 0,25 is bigger than 0,5 because 25 is bigger than 5, or place the decimal comma in the wrong place.

topics.name: Two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects
misconceptions: Learners may think a square is not a rectangle, or count faces, edges and corners on a drawing as if it were the real object.

topics.name: Capacity and mass
misconceptions: Learners may think a taller container always holds more, or confuse mass with how much space something takes up.

topics.name: Number patterns and number sentences
misconceptions: Learners may continue a pattern by copying the last step instead of finding the rule, or put the missing number only at the end of the sentence.

topics.name: Money and simple budgets
prerequisites: Addition and subtraction of larger numbers
misconceptions: Learners may forget that 100 cents make one rand, or think change is found by adding the cost and the amount given.

topics.name: Data handling
misconceptions: Learners may draw bars without a scale, or read a pictograph by counting pictures instead of using the key.

topics.name: Position and movement
misconceptions: Learners may mix up left and right depending on who is looking at the map, or think north always means up on the page.

leftOut.name: Percentages
leftOut.reason: The plan says percentages belong to Grade 7 and are not taught in Grade 5.
